note: Canonical hue ranges for intent colors. These are culturally load-bearing — a 'success' color outside the green-cyan band will read as wrong in Western contexts. Each family can shift ±tolerance to fit brand voice but must remain within its band.

danger.rationale: Red-orange band. Pure red (0°) can feel aggressive; a slight orange shift (15°–30°) reads as 'urgent' without hostility.

warning.rationale: Yellow-amber band. Pure yellow (90°) has very low contrast on light surfaces; anchor toward amber (70°–80°) for legibility.

success.rationale: Green band. 150° is perceptually balanced (between emerald and lime). Below 135° reads yellow-green (ambiguous); above 165° reads teal.

info.rationale: Blue band. Avoid the brand accent's hue by at least 20° if the brand is blue — otherwise info reads as 'brand' and loses its semantic distinctness.

collisionRule: No two intent colors may share a hue within ±20°. No intent may share a hue within ±20° of the brand accent (success/info are the most likely collisions).
